items.title: Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards actually goes live in beta: zero data retention, keys held in your own cloud bucket
items.summary: Anthropic first announced EFS on Sept 1 as a phased rollout "later this fall"; Claude Platform release notes now show it landed in beta on Nov 23. Anthropic stops retaining prompts and responses; an encrypted copy is written to a storage bucket the customer owns, unreadable even by the customer's own team, with Anthropic's human review permanently off. Live now on Claude Platform (per workspace) and via Amazon Bedrock.
items.why: The most concrete answer yet to "how do we get frontier-model capability without handing our prompts to the vendor."
items.action: If your company has held off on top-tier models over data-retention concerns, check EFS eligibility and study the bucket-ownership model as a pattern for anything sensitive you build.

items.title: LangSmith Tool Gateway (Public Beta): one managed layer for agent tool credentials, approvals, and audit trails
items.summary: Centralizes how agents authenticate to and call tools: register MCP or built-in servers into "tool kits" at one URL, choose whether an agent acts as itself or the signed-in user, set deny/approval policies requiring human confirmation for sensitive calls, and get full tool-call traces. The example customer, a large US retailer building store-ops agents, has already stood up 50+ MCP servers exposing over 1,000 tools through it.
items.why: Answers "which agent, posing as which identity, is allowed to call which tool, and can I prove it after" -- the gap that stops a demo from getting signed off by security.
items.action: If you run more than a couple of MCP servers behind an agent, look specifically at the approval-policy model for sensitive calls.

items.title: Why Cloudflare Became a Neolab -- Michelle Chen, Cloudflare
items.summary: Cloudflare bet early that models would stay small enough to run at the edge; they grew to trillions of parameters instead, so Cloudflare pivoted to serving frontier models. Then fast "decision models" for prompt routing arrived, and Cloudflare trained its own from scratch over a weekend, shipping four models in a few days.
items.why: A fast-turnaround case study in the same decision-model pattern as a recent LangChain pick -- useful for how quickly a team can stand one up.
